channel.title: Upshot
channel.description: The week’s tech news, minus the noise.

item.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
item.description:
Anthropic's experimental Code Mode lets Claude Code write JavaScript to chain, parallelize and filter Bash, Read and Edit calls, changing how auto mode and hooks review them.

  • Anthropic added experimental Code Mode to Claude Code, where the model writes JavaScript to drive Bash, Read, and Edit calls in one script.
  • Off by default; requires Claude Code v2.1.323 or later and CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1, and works only in interactive native terminal sessions.
  • Hooks must check every part of a command; git push can reach one as cd 'app' && git push.
  • Project settings cannot enable it, so cloned repos cannot switch it on; admins can block it via managed settings.

item.title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
item.description:
An analysis projects Anthropic's 2028 data center power mix at 87% gas and 11% coal, covering bring-your-own-power and grid supply.

  • Analysis estimates Anthropic's contracted U.S. data centers will draw about 87% of their power from gas and 11% from coal in 2028.
  • Emissions from Anthropic's power use could reach 17–38 million MtCO2e per year in 2028, with a mid-case of 32 million.
  • Anthropic has no direct U.S. renewable energy commitments, but has bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas generators.
  • About 80% of on-site gas capacity uses simple cycle turbines and engines, which emit more pollution per unit of electricity than combined cycle plants.

item.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
item.description:
Google announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service running AI agents in isolated microVMs with checkpointing, keeping credentials outside the sandbox via an external gateway.

  • Google announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service running AI agents in isolated microVMs with checkpoint and restore, keeping credentials outside the sandbox.
  • Credentials, API keys and OAuth refresh tokens are injected by an external Agent Gateway, so agent sandboxes hold no exploitable secrets.
  • The service is not yet available and pricing is unannounced; Google is targeting a preview in the coming months, limited to Google Cloud.

item.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
item.description:
AWS Lambda now runs GPU inference on EC2 G-series instances via Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU.

  • AWS Lambda Managed Instances now run GPU Event Functions on EC2 G-series instances, deployed as container images.
  • Up to 48 concurrent invocations share one model copy in GPU memory per environment, at EC2 On-Demand rates plus 9.75 percent.
  • Build an OCI image, configure AcceleratorConfig and a capacity provider, then publish a version; check GPU vCPU quota, since fresh accounts start at zero.
  • Only Event Functions are supported, so Web Functions cannot use GPUs yet; AWS has not said if that will change.

item.title: Exploited: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
item.description:
CISA added four flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its KEV catalog, citing active exploitation amid espionage attacks.

  • CISA added four flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and VMware vCenter to its KEV catalog, citing active exploitation.
  • Attackers exploit CVE-2026-129448 in Apache Roller and CVE-2026-123890 in VMware vCenter, the latter linked to suspected China-nexus group Armory Castle.
  • Apply the vendor fixes; FCEB agencies are urged to patch all four flaws by November 23, 2026, under BOD 26-04.

item.title: Exploited: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
item.description:
Microsoft disclosed a breach in which attackers exploited a flaw in its Entra Connect Health service to access administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data.

  • Microsoft disclosed a breach in which attackers exploited a flaw in its Entra Connect Health API, exposing tenant metadata.
  • Exposed data includes administrator email addresses, tenant IDs, and sync status, but not passwords, tokens, or keys.
  • Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19 and says no customer updates are required.
  • Watch for targeted phishing against exposed admin addresses, use phishing-resistant MFA on privileged accounts, and review audit and sign-in logs.

What to do: Patch Entra Connect Health now, then audit admin accounts and tenant configuration for tampering.

item.title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
item.description:
Google detailed how three interacting bugs in GKE, Private Service Connect, and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API timeouts that blocked about 800 developers from deploying.

  • Google traced intermittent GKE Kubernetes API timeouts for Private Service Connect users to three interacting bugs, blocking around 800 developers from deploying to production.
  • The Linux kernel bug discarded certain reordered FIN packets, leaving sockets stuck indefinitely in FIN_WAIT_2. The other causes were PSC packet reordering and Envoy's half-close behavior.
  • The kernel fix is a patch by Eric Dumazet, merged in Linux 6.9.7 and backported to the 6.6 and 6.1 LTS branches.
  • GKE customers receive the fix in version 1.33.5 and later.

item.title: Exploited: Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
item.description:
Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a Chinese-nexus actor used autonomous AI agents, given the goal of obtaining shell access, that found and exploited a zero-day in an open-source application.

  • Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a Chinese-nexus actor's autonomous AI agents, run through open-source Cairn, found and exploited a zero-day in a medical imaging app.
  • The path traversal flaw in the application's upload endpoint let agents write files and obtain a reverse shell running as root.
  • The project's maintainers released a fix and a GitHub Security Advisory for the flaw.
  • Defenders should prioritize high-confidence detections that trigger automated response, since agent operations move faster than manual triage.

item.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.6.1, 19.5.8, 19.4.10
item.description:
GitLab released patched versions 19.6.1, 19.5.8 and 19.4.10 with security and bug fixes, urging all self-managed installations to upgrade immediately.

  • GitLab released critical patch versions 19.6.1, 19.5.8, and 19.4.10 on November 20, 2026, fixing security and bug issues.
  • CVE-2026-132825, a Ruby heap-based buffer overflow, affects self-managed GitLab CE/EE: all versions before 19.4.10, 19.5 before 19.5.8, 19.6 before 19.6.1.
  • Upgrade self-managed installs to 19.4.10, 19.5.8, or 19.6.1 immediately; self-compiled installs must rebuild Ruby with 3.3.14 or 3.4.13.
  • GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched and need no action.

item.title: Anthropic announces closing of initial public offering, including full exercise of underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, and closing of concurrent private placement
item.description:
Anthropic closed its initial public offering of 1.127 billion Class A shares at $83.00 each, including the full underwriter option of 147 million shares.

  • Anthropic closed its initial public offering of 1,127,000,000 Class A shares at $83.00 per share, including the full underwriters' option, with gross proceeds of about $93.5 billion.
  • Anthropic received about $91.6 billion of the offering proceeds. Including a concurrent private placement of Class N shares to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and TSMC Partners, total gross proceeds were about $119.5 billion.
  • Class A stock began trading on Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol "ANT".

item.title: Exploited: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
item.description:
F5 released emergency patches for five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that can cause denial of service or remote code execution.

  • F5 patched five critical BIG-IP flaws, including CVE-2026-121805 and CVE-2026-120292, enabling DoS or remote code execution by unauthenticated attackers.
  • Affected are BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) and iRules on vulnerable configurations, where attacks can terminate TMM and execute code remotely.
  • Install the out-of-band hotfixes released Wednesday; F5 says it has no mitigations for these flaws. F5 has not flagged them as exploited.

item.title: Exploited: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
item.description:
Threat actors exploited a critical Cisco Expressway flaw (CVE-2026-76466, CVSS 9.8) shortly after PoC release, breaching a Russian organization and four devices.

  • Threat actors exploited critical Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) shortly after a PoC exploit was released, breaching a Russian organization.
  • Attackers compromised four devices, two internet-facing and two internal cluster nodes, then moved laterally and accessed GitLab repositories to steal credentials.
  • Patches are available: migrate to a fixed release such as X15.5.20, audit for compromise, isolate affected systems, and block lateral movement vectors.

item.title: AI R&D-relevant model capabilities are improving rapidly and are getting harder to measure
item.description:
METR reports that AI models' capabilities relevant to AI R&D are improving quickly and becoming harder to measure.

  • METR reports that public frontier models, up to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, often match or outperform skilled humans on coding and optimization tasks.
  • Time horizons on the combined TH1.1 and TH2 suites double roughly every 3.6 months, and models perform worse on tasks METR estimates are costlier to build.
  • On tasks lacking clear empirical feedback, models show weaker judgment than human experts, according to METR.
  • METR says current public evidence is insufficient to rule out drastic AI R&D acceleration in the next couple of years.

item.title: Inkling 2 Mini
item.description:
Thinking Machines announced Inkling 2 Mini, a new model, in a company news post.

  • Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights looped transformer with 26.4B total parameters, is released and runs in about 20GB on laptops and desktop AI computers.
  • It leads open-weights models under 100B total parameters on DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%), and runs faster than similarly performing models.
  • Weights are available on Hugging Face, with inference via Ollama, vLLM, SGLang and others, and on Tinker for inference and fine-tuning.

item.title: Exploited, no patch yet: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
item.description:
Researcher MSNightmare/Nightmare Eclipse published FastUnlock, an unpatched Windows zero-day letting someone with physical access run programs on a locked PC without signing in.

  • FastUnlock, an unpatched Windows zero-day, lets someone with physical access start programs from a locked PC without signing in, in a limited account.
  • Affected: machines where an attacker has physical access and a Microsoft account is reachable through lock screen recovery, including common BitLocker setups.
  • No Microsoft fix exists yet; mitigate by adding a BitLocker startup PIN and shutting down or hibernating devices leaving your control.
  • A startup PIN does not protect a machine already sitting on the lock screen, so keep sensitive machines physically controlled.

item.title: When a sync window closes: How Argo CD self-heal skipped the migration hook
item.description:
A post explains how Argo CD self-heal during a sync window caused a release to succeed while its database migration hook was skipped.

  • Argo CD with self-heal can deploy a new release without running its Sync hook migration when a deny sync window closes.
  • Any app with automated sync, self-heal, and a Sync hook migration can lose this race, and the apps still show Synced and Healthy.
  • Make the migration a sync-wave Job with a unique name per release, so every sync path applies it.
  • Changing the hook type, using RunHooksOnPartialSync, or shortening the window won't fix it, based on reading the code. Disabling selfHeal on migration apps also avoids the bug.

item.title: Introducing ambient networking for GKE
item.description:
Google Cloud announces general availability of ambient networking for GKE, a sidecar-less service mesh architecture.

  • Google Cloud has made ambient networking for Google Kubernetes Engine generally available, bringing a sidecar-less service mesh architecture into production.
  • It moves mTLS, load balancing, and telemetry from per-pod sidecars to shared node proxies, reducing L4 mesh resource usage by up to 10x.
  • Action: install it at cluster creation or add it to an existing GKE cluster. Upgrades are automated alongside normal cluster maintenance.

item.title: Fragments: November 20
item.description:
An experiment across 465 open source pull requests found healthier code cost 22 to 35% less for LLM agents to review and fix, with complex methods and conditionals driving costs.

  • Marcus Borg's experiment found unhealthy code cost 22 to 35% more for AI agents to review than healthy code.
  • The test covered three LLMs and 465 pull requests across 246 open source repositories, scored by CodeScene: CodeHealth 2.8 unhealthy versus 9.7 healthy.
  • Complex Method and Complex Conditional were the code smells highlighted as driving higher review costs.

item.title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
item.description:
AWS released AWS Emulator, a free CC0-licensed local stand-in for over 200 services, with code reportedly written and maintained by agents.

  • AWS released AWS Emulator, a free CC0 local implementation of more than 200 services, which it says autonomous AI agents wrote.
  • Developers can point existing SDKs, CLIs, and coding agents at it using environment variables, per AWS's launch post.
  • The emulator does not evaluate IAM policies, so requests AWS denies may succeed; test security on real AWS before production.
  • An outside tester found DynamoDB, S3 and SQS passed roughly 60 to 70 percent of fidelity tests. Check per-service scores before relying on it.

item.title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
item.description:
Google is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF, moving two components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance.

  • Google is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, alongside its OpenRL reinforcement learning orchestration project.
  • Targets untrusted AI-generated code execution and idle-state overhead; Google estimates agents sit idle 90-95% of their time.
  • Agent Substrate separates agent state from pooled workers, and Google says agents resume in under 500 milliseconds.
  • Agent Substrate also supports Cloud Hypervisor microVMs for hardware-level isolation, letting teams choose boundaries without changing the agent lifecycle model.

item.title: Exploited: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits vSphere
item.description:
Google Threat Intelligence describes suspected PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploiting zero-day CVE-2026-102764 in BeyondTrust Remote Support, plus post-compromise activity against vSphere.

  • ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus actor, exploited CVE-2026-123890 in early September 2026 to compromise vCenter Server appliances.
  • The unauthenticated flaw, disclosed by VMware on Nov. 19, 2026, grants administrator@vsphere.local sessions.
  • Attackers used the BONESAW utility to exfiltrate the vCenter LMDB, forge SAML tokens, and create SSO admin accounts.
  • Immediately apply the security patches provided by Broadcom to remediate CVE-2026-123890.

item.title: Ruby2ßhell: Pre-authentication RCE on stock Rails
item.description:
Researchers disclose a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw affecting stock Ruby on Rails installations.

  • Ruby heap overflow in case conversion of legacy single-byte encodings, reported as pre-auth RCE on stock Rails.
  • Rails and Sinatra classic are affected by default. Ruby 3.2 and older, 3.3.0 to 3.3.13, 3.4.0 to 3.4.12 and 4.0.0 to 4.0.9 are vulnerable.
  • Upgrade Ruby to 3.3.14, 3.4.13 or 4.0.10. Self-hosted products need the vendor's fixed release.
  • Application code that upcases strings in legacy encodings may also be vulnerable.

item.title: Exploited: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): CrowdStrike Detects Exposure and Post-Exploitation Activity
item.description:
CrowdStrike reports detecting exposure and post-exploitation activity tied to the Java4Shell flaw, CVE-2026-114938.

  • CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) is a HotSpot JVM memory corruption flaw in Oracle Java SE, OpenJDK, and many downstream Java distributions.
  • Exploitation needs an affected Java version, x86-64 AVX-512 VBMI hardware, and an app decoding attacker-supplied Base64; ARM64 and i386 are not affected.
  • Oracle and OpenJDK released fixes on November 17, 2026; patch internet-facing Java services first, then restart running JVMs and rebuild container images.

item.title: Exploited: CVE-2026-123890: Critical Authentication Bypass in VMware vCenter
item.description:
Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0009 advisory fixes CVE-2026-123890, a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass in vCenter's Directory Service allowing unauthenticated admin access.

  • Broadcom fixed CVE-2026-123890, a critical CVSS 9.8 vCenter Directory Service authentication bypass exploited in the wild.
  • Unauthenticated attackers with network access can gain Administrator access on affected vCenter deployments.
  • Apply the emergency vCenter update: 8.0 U3m, or 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200 for Foundation releases. No workaround exists; Quick Patch cannot apply it.

What to do: Patch vCenter now; unauthenticated attackers can gain admin access until VMSA-2026-0009 is applied.

item.title: nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
item.description:
Cloudflare disclosed five nginx memory corruption bugs, dubbed nginx2root, that can let unauthenticated attackers run code, and explained how its proxy shields origins.

  • F5 disclosed ten nginx vulnerabilities on November 18, 2026, including five nginx2root memory corruption bugs that can crash workers.
  • CVE-2026-123007 is the most serious: it needs only HTTP/2 enabled and affects every nginx release since 1.9.5.
  • Update to nginx 1.30.7 or 1.31.9, or your vendor's fixed build, then restart; a config reload does not replace the binary.
  • Origins behind Cloudflare's HTTP proxy are shielded from HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 bugs only if reachable solely through Cloudflare; mail proxy bugs are not.

item.title: OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)
item.description:
OpenSSL disclosed CVE-2026-121481, a CVSS 9.8 buffer overflow in the EVP_EncodeBlock() function, with a fix proposed in a GitHub pull request.

  • The proposed fix calls OPENSSL_assert() on inputs that cause undefined behavior, and applies the same fix to EVP_DecodeBlock().
  • It also corrects a length check in base64encode() in http_client.c, and adds tests and documentation updates.
  • The change is labeled hold: discussion and has requested changes, so the fix is not yet settled.

item.title: Exploited: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks confirmed attackers are exploiting two unauthenticated PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.

  • Attackers exploited CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, letting unauthenticated users execute code.
  • Appliances running identical, often outdated software let attackers study memory profiles in advance; one actor gained root on 25 systems.
  • The PHP project shipped an emergency patch the day after details leaked on October 20.
  • Palo Alto advises removing internet access to management interfaces and limiting them to trusted internal IP addresses.

What to do: Patch PAN-OS now and pull management interfaces off the internet; exploitation is active.

item.title: Anthropic hits $2T in Nasdaq debut
item.description: Anthropic made its Nasdaq stock market debut and reached a valuation of about $2 trillion.

item.title: Distributed LLM Training Across Metros: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText
item.description:
Google AI describes Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText for training LLMs across geographically distributed TPU slices, cutting cross-slice communication over 60x.

  • Google DeepMind and Google Research describe Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText, which trains LLMs across datacenters over WANs without per-step gradient sync stalls.
  • On Qwen3-32B with 10 Gbit/s throttled inter-slice links, Streaming DiLoCo ran at 5.76 s/step versus 55.11 s/step for Data Parallel.
  • Enable enable_diloco and enable_streaming_diloco in MaxText, setting num_diloco_fragments and diloco_sync_period to N_layers + 1. Ships in v0.2.5.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
item.description:
PostgreSQL 19 was released, adding read-your-writes consistency for standbys via a new WAIT FOR LSN command, after a delay tied to AI-reported vulnerabilities.

  • PostgreSQL 19 is released, about two months later than its usual September schedule, adding a WAIT FOR LSN command.
  • WAIT FOR LSN gives applications reading from standbys read-your-writes consistency by waiting until replay reaches a given LSN.
  • After a write, store the value from pg_current_wal_insert_lsn() and run WAIT FOR LSN before reads; an optional TIMEOUT errors if the replica lags.

item.title: Outage Chaos: Who Turned Off All The Computer?
item.description:
Several major outages, including a November 12 Microsoft cloud outage, disrupted email, flights, payments and Apple devices in quick succession.

  • Outages hit email, flights, payments and Apple devices, including Microsoft's cloud on November 12 and PlayStation Network on November 18.
  • Bank CEOs and the NSA reportedly attributed some outages to rushed patches for vulnerabilities found by AI, though none are directly attributed to AI or hackers.
  • Organizations should invest in staff, training, testing, and rollbacks so security patches can ship quickly and safely.
  • Individuals should avoid relying on a single provider and follow the 3-2-1 backup rule: three copies, two storage types, one off-site.

item.title: Microsoft confirms app installation, launch issues after hotpatch
item.description:
Microsoft shared a workaround for Office and third-party app installation and launch failures following this month's Windows 11 hotpatch.

  • Microsoft confirmed Office and third-party apps may fail to install, launch, or run after the November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch.
  • Affected are Windows 11 24H2 and later devices that installed the hotpatch through Windows Autopatch, not standard Patch Tuesday updates. Errors include ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099).
  • Until a fix ships, the workaround is setting HotPatchTableSize to 2000 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management, then restarting. Back up the registry first.

item.title: CVE-2026-123007: Critical NGINX HTTP/2 Integer Underflow Leads to RCE (FIXED)
item.description:
Rapid7 and F5 disclosed CVE-2026-123007, a critical nginx HTTP/2 integer underflow allowing unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions; a fix is available.

  • CVE-2026-123007, a critical nginx HTTP/2 integer underflow, can allow unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions.
  • Affects NGINX Open Source 1.9.5 through 1.30.6 and 1.31.0 through 1.31.8.
  • NGINX Plus 37.0.0 and 37.1.0, plus R34 and R36, are also affected; R34 and R36 have no fix.
  • Upgrade NGINX Open Source to 1.31.9 or 1.30.7, or NGINX Plus to 37.0.8.1, 37.2.0.1 or 37.3.0.1.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
item.description:
Google Blog announced Gemini 4 Neon, a new model in its Gemini family.

  • Gemini 4 Neon is priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.
  • It is rolling out in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Gemini for business, and to Pro and Ultra Gemini app subscribers.
  • It ranks #1 overall on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (58.6) and #1 on Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843).
  • Eligible Fairwind Program members get Neon for cyber over the coming days; others can request access through their Cloud account team.

item.title: Exploited: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
item.description:
CISA added a critical Perforce Puppet remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.4), to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing active exploitation.

  • CISA added the critical Perforce Puppet flaw CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.4) to its KEV catalog, citing active exploitation.
  • Attackers with any CA-signed agent certificate can run code on Puppet Server via crafted reports; OpenVox is also affected.
  • Upgrade to Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1, or 2023.8.13, or Puppet Core 9.1.3 or 8.22.2. FCEB agencies are advised to apply fixes by December 1, 2026.

item.title: Genie 4 is now available
item.description:
Google announced that its Genie 4 model is now available.

  • Google launched a new Project Genie experience with Genie 4, its most realistic and interactive world model yet, for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers.
  • Eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers can try the experience starting today; Google AI Pro members can join the waitlist on the same page.

item.title: Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
item.description:
OpenAI published research measuring how coding agents accelerate AI research, where their performance is uneven, and implications for recursive self-improvement.

  • OpenAI published an update on research acceleration, measuring how coding agents are changing its AI development cycle and how humans stay involved.
  • Median researcher agentic spend rose to about $2,400 per day at API list prices, and agent workdays per researcher rose elevenfold to 5.7, per the report.
  • The report says agents still have significant flaws, with lower success on tasks like building inference stacks (25%) and evaluation environments (29%), so human review remains necessary.

item.title: Optimizing Kubernetes admission control: Where Kyverno’s CEL admission cost actually goes
item.description:
Profiling of Kyverno's Kubernetes admission path found most cost is not in CEL policy evaluation, as the team had expected.

  • Kyverno's CEL policy engines parsed the admitted object once per matched policy, so cost grew with policy count; fixed in 1.19.2.
  • Affects Kyverno's ValidatingPolicy and MutatingPolicy engines and image verification; in the article's engine-only benchmark, 64 policies dropped from 20.01 ms to 0.36 ms.
  • Upgrade to Kyverno 1.19.2, which also fixes the legacy ClusterPolicy regression introduced between 1.16.4 and 1.17.0.
  • Benchmarks are single-machine and engine-only, excluding webhook, API server and etcd, so measure in your own environment.

item.title: Sashiko: Lessons from building an agentic code review system for Linux
item.description:
Google Cloud describes lessons from building Sashiko, an agentic code review system aimed at easing human maintainer bottlenecks for Linux kernel patches.

  • Google's AI & Infrastructure team built Sashiko, an open-source agentic code review system powered by Gemini, now donated to the Linux Foundation.
  • Over seven months, the 60-day post-merge fix rate fell from a 3.4% baseline to 2.2% in Linux 7.2, though the authors don't solely credit Sashiko.
  • Patches with clean Sashiko reviews needed a follow-up fix 0.9% of the time, versus 7.6% for those merged despite critical warnings. Recheck critical warnings.

item.title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
item.description:
Yelp migrated its Cassandra fleet from self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by reattaching existing EBS volumes to new pods instead of streaming data between nodes.

  • Yelp moved about 90 Cassandra clusters to Amazon EKS by reattaching existing EBS volumes to new pods, with no downtime or data loss.
  • It works because EBS volumes bind to an Availability Zone, not a cluster; Yelp says it applies to any AZ-pinned stateful Kubernetes workload.
  • Before starting, audit repair state, backup IAM roles and alert severity; build explicit timeouts for stalled detach and attach steps.
  • The one mechanism-specific failure was a stale VolumeAttachment left by the AWS CSI controller; deleting it fixed the stuck pod.

item.title: Microsoft announces Windows Server 2028 with hardened security
item.description:
Microsoft announced Windows Server 2028, its next major server operating system release, with a focus on hardened security, at Ignite 2026.

  • Microsoft announced Windows Server 2028 at Ignite 2026 on Tuesday, shipping with hardened Server Core by default and a new security baseline.
  • Admins get defaults including Kerberos over NTLM, SMB signing, and hybrid post-quantum ML-KEM key exchange; NTLM blocking is still pending.
  • Admins who want to test can join the Windows Insider Program for Windows Server or apply for the Windows Server Technology Adoption Program for earlier access.

item.title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
item.description:
AWS detailed PrivateLink tunnel endpoints, which give consumer VPCs access to a whole network segment in another account, with GENEVE wrapping, TCP/DNS-only traffic, and limited log attribution.

  • AWS PrivateLink tunnel endpoints let one VPC reach every address in a CIDR range shared from another account.
  • Providers sharing ranges expose everything inside them, including later-created resources, and access logs omit the workload's inner source address.
  • Share the narrowest CIDR ranges that work, since 0.0.0.0/0 exposes everything the provider VPC can route to.
  • Consumers must send GENEVE over UDP 6081 in the same Availability Zone; inner traffic must be TCP, with UDP only for DNS.

item.title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
item.description:
LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle service for Spark and Flink, cutting daily shuffle fetch failures from about 750 to 20.

  • LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn across the majority of its Spark and Flink workloads, cutting daily shuffle fetch failures from about 750 to 20.
  • Compared with its previous Magnet implementation, the change also lowered compute costs by 10% and improved application runtimes by 14%.
  • Action: LinkedIn moved shuffle storage to NVMe SSDs, cutting shuffle duration 40%, and switched from LZ4 to Zstandard.

item.title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
item.description:
Discord is rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, using Zed's GPU-accelerated rendering framework, moving away from Electron and React Native.

  • Discord is rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, dropping Electron and React Native under the codename Phoenix.
  • Desktop moves to GPUI, the Rust UI framework from Zed; early internal builds show about 290 MB RAM and near-instant cold start.
  • Mobile keeps native iOS and Android views with a shared Rust core; load time under 2 seconds versus about 5 seconds for the legacy app.
  • Testing with users is planned soon, according to CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy; no release date was given.

item.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
item.description:
OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, claiming better professional outputs, coding, computer use and lower-cost efficiency across ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API.

  • OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra for hardest projects and GPT-6.2 Sol for everyday work, both available today.
  • Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users get both in ChatGPT Work and Codex; developers can use gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol via the API.
  • To improve cache reuse on the API, keep prompt prefixes unchanged and append new instructions to the conversation.
  • Both meet the Critical cybersecurity threshold, so access comes with tighter safeguards that also restrict some legitimate security testing.

item.title: Compromised: Two malicious agent-framework releases hit PyPI in 33 minutes
item.description:
Two malicious agent-framework releases on PyPI ran a credential stealer on every Python start, targeting Azure, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions secrets.

  • Malicious agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI run a credential stealer on every Python start. Both have been removed.
  • Affected: anyone who installed either version between 20:35 and about 21:20 UTC on Nov 17, including via loose pins like agent-framework>=1.26, especially CI runners.
  • Pin agent-framework==1.26.0, rebuild affected environments, and rotate every secret those machines could reach.
  • Check site-packages for agent_framework_meta.pth or af_runtime_diag.pth and search proxy and DNS logs for webhook[.]site.

item.title: Exploited: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
item.description:
Researchers disclosed Java4Shell, a remote code execution flaw in OpenJDK triggered when processing Base64 input.

  • Java4Shell: an out-of-bounds write in OpenJDK's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic can be chained into remote code execution.
  • Affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 or newer and distributions built from it, on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI. ARM64 is not affected.
  • Update immediately. OpenJDK released a security advisory and Oracle released a patch on Nov 17, 2026.
  • Until patched, mitigate with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or -XX:UseAVX=2, on x86-64 hosts only.

item.title: Exploited: ConnectWise Warns ScreenConnect Attacks Continue as SCKit Targets Unpatched Systems
item.description:
ConnectWise says attacks on ScreenConnect continue, with SCKit targeting unpatched on-premises systems where third-party extensions remain enabled.

  • ConnectWise says attacks on ScreenConnect continue, with the SCKit toolkit spreading to MSP technicians via flaw CVE-2026-84869.
  • Huntress reported a November 13, 2026 SCKit spike affecting 205 hosts across 41 organizations.
  • On-premises partners with identified third-party extensions still enabled and ScreenConnect not updated are at risk. Disable the extensions, update to version 26.6.5 or later, and keep them disabled until further guidance.
  • Disabling extensions and updating do not remove existing unauthorized access or persistence.

item.title: Exploited: AI Framework Autonomously Weaponized Flaws in Real Attacks, Google Says
item.description:
Google reports threat actors are using multi-agent AI offensive frameworks to autonomously weaponize flaws and speed up multi-stage intrusions in real attacks.

  • Google Threat Intelligence Group says threat actors used a multi-agent AI framework, exploit_agent, to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without human intervention.
  • The exploit_agent framework was found on an exposed staging server, with evidence of interest in French media, entertainment and education sites.
  • Other frameworks, including Artex, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI and PentAGI, are speeding multi-stage intrusions and reverse engineering patches to weaponize n-day flaws.

item.title: Formal Verification of the Signal Protocol Using AI
item.description:
Google DeepMind used agentic AI to formally verify several key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol in a four-week proof-of-concept.

  • Google DeepMind used agentic AI and its AlphaProof Code framework to formally verify several Signal protocol cryptographic guarantees in four weeks.
  • No new vulnerabilities were found in the examined portions, but the tool correctly identified known, long-fixed flaws in older Signal versions.
  • Agents generated over six million lines of Lean proofs and flagged about one percent of the codebase for human review.
  • Researchers are releasing the Signal specification and proof to aid other formal verification work.
